key_insight: Modeling when and why humans intervene lets web agents decide to defer, ask, or act autonomously—reducing unnecessary confirmations and preventing errors at critical decision points.
problem_solved: Agents currently lack a principled model of human intervention, causing them to either act past important decisions or request unneeded human confirmation; this work formalizes and models intervention behavior to support smoother human–agent collaboration in web tasks.
method: Collect CowCorpus: a curated dataset of human–agent web task interactions annotated for intervention timing and reasons.
Train intervention models that predict (a) whether a human will intervene and (b) the likely reason/intention, using contextual signals from the agent’s state and task history.
Integrate intervention predictions into agent decision policies (defer/query/proceed) and compare performance to baseline autonomous and always-query behaviors.
impact: Provides practitioners with a dataset and modeling approach to make web agents more reliable, efficient, and trustworthy by enabling context-aware human-in-the-loop decisions—reducing error rates and unnecessary user interruptions.
visual_elements: Dataset schematic: overview of CowCorpus composition (sessions, intervention labels, reason categories).
Timeline diagram: agent actions vs. predicted intervention points and ground-truth human interventions.
Bar chart or ROC: model performance vs. baselines on intervention detection and reason classification.
Flowchart: how intervention predictions change agent decisions (proceed / ask / defer) in a task loop.
paper_title: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
paper_authors: Faria Huq, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Zhanqiu Guo, Venu Arvind Arangarajan, Tianyue Ou
